references.text: The creation account uses the same expression 'after its kind' (לְמִינֵהוּ) as in Gen 6:20, showing that Noah was to preserve all the kinds God had created.
Describes the actual fulfillment of God's instruction: the animals came to Noah in pairs on the ark, two by two, male and female.
Details how the animals came to the ark in pairs after their kind—birds, livestock, and creeping things—in direct fulfillment of the instruction in 6:20.
Expands on the instruction to bring animals into the ark, specifying clean and unclean animals as well as birds.
The Hebrews describe Noah's faith: he obeyed God's instructions in reverence and built the ark for the salvation of his household.
Complementary commands regarding the preservation (entry) and restoration (release) of the animals in the flood narrative.
A literary parallel showing that the flood functions as a new creation, where God's original word about preserving the kinds is repeated.
6:20 ensures the preservation of the created order established in the creation account.
Direct continuation and clarification of the command regarding the number of animals (seven pairs versus two) for clean species in the flood.
Theological contrast between God's saving of the animals (6:20) and humanity's new authority over them (9:2) after the flood.
